claims.claim_ar: حصر بالاستثناء بواسطة أداة «إِلَّا» في «مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ» لإظهار التخصيص والتأكيد
claims.claim_en: Restriction/exclusion by the particle 'إِلَّا' in "مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ", indicating specification and emphasis (hasr/qasr).

claims.claim_ar: مقابلة/توافق بياني بين «الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً» و«الْقَمَرَ نُورًا»: تراكيب موازية توزِع المعنى على عنصرين كونيين لإظهار النظام والتناسب
claims.claim_en: Parallelism/paired balance between 'الشَّمْسَ ضِياءً' and 'الْقَمَرَ نُورًا': parallel structures attributing complementary roles to two celestial bodies, highlighting order and proportion.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source quote discusses a similar pairing in another passage; mapping this general notion of pairing to the Sun/Moon expressions of this ayah is interpretive and should be reviewed.

claims.claim_ar: استعمال فعل «جَعَلَ» لبيان التعيين والعلّية (جعل + مفعول) في «جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً»، أي: تَقرِيرُ الله تعيين وظيفة/حالة للشمس كسبب أو وسيلة.
claims.claim_en: Use of the verb 'جَعَلَ' to express assignment/causation (make/appoint) as a stylistic device in 'جَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ ضِيَاءً', i.e. marking God's assignment of function/state to the sun.
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted explanation in the source addresses the rhetorical effect of using جعل in another context; applying it to this ayah is plausible but interpretive and merits review.

warnings: The provided source_chunks are from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) and al-Tabari; the requested authors (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, tafsir balagha) were not included. Claims below therefore rely on the available chunks and on general Qur'anic-rhetorical correspondence rather than explicit quotations from the named authors.

Some claims map general rhetorical observations from the supplied commentaries (which discuss other verses/patterns) onto this ayah; these mappings are interpretive and flagged in needs_review_reason where appropriate.

No explicit substrings from the supplied chunks contained an exact commentary phrase for every rhetorical point in this ayah; where a direct match was unavailable, only conservative claims (with medium confidence) were made.
